title: When the Static Wakes
premise: Ulyana Lockridge, a xenolinguist whose mind was rewired by an alien signal she decoded years ago, discovers that the colony's children are dreaming in that same language — a countdown transmitted through the sleep of a generation. The signal originates from the cryo-vaults holding half the colony's original settlers, where a ruling council has been secretly deciding who deserves to wake. Ulyana, her estranged brother Dario (the council's enforcer), and a dream-touched child named Sefa must expose the council's corruption and choose which half of humanity wakes — before the vault's failing power grid makes the choice for them. In the end, Ulyana sacrifices her own place in the waking world, translating herself into the signal to become the bridge between the sleepers and the born, while the children who dreamed the countdown open the vaults to everyone the council condemned.
about_author: Edmund Winterbourne is the pen name of a former radio engineer who spent a decade maintaining deep-space relay stations before turning to fiction. His work blends hard orbital mechanics with the quiet terror of voices received from nowhere.

chapters.title: The Language Under Sleep
chapters.summary: Ulyana, hauling ore through contested orbits, dreams again in the alien signal she decoded seven years ago — the first time in years her sleep speaks anything at all. POV: Ulyana. Beat: unease, the sense that something old has found her.

chapters.title: Cargo and Quiet
chapters.summary: Docking at Meridian Station, Ulyana notices dockworkers' children drawing the same spiraling glyph on crates. She recognizes her own transcription symbols. POV: Ulyana. Beat: creeping recognition.

chapters.title: The Council's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dario Lockridge, enforcer for the Settlement Council, audits the cryo-vault's power draw and finds a falsified maintenance record. His supervisor warns him to log it as routine. POV: Dario. Beat: first crack in loyalty.

chapters.title: Sefa Counts Backward
chapters.summary: Sefa, an eight-year-old born on-station, tells her teacher the dream has a number in it, and the number is smaller every night. The teacher reports it; the report vanishes. POV: Sefa. Beat: innocence meeting institutional silence.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Static
chapters.summary: Flashback: Ulyana's first contact with the signal aboard the survey ship Calloway, the decoding that rewired her language centers, and the inquiry that ended her career. POV: Ulyana. Beat: grief and vindication deferred.

chapters.title: The Children's Chorus
chapters.summary: Ulyana interviews eleven dreaming children; each recites fragments that assemble into a coherent grammar — and a timestamp. She realizes the signal is counting down to a vault event. POV: Ulyana. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Brother, Gatekeeper
chapters.summary: Ulyana approaches Dario at the vault perimeter. He refuses her access but pockets the glyph she shows him, shaken by its familiarity from council briefings. POV: Dario. Beat: torn between blood and badge.

chapters.title: Who Sleeps, Who Wakes
chapters.summary: The council meets to finalize Wake Priority List revisions. Chair Odile Voss argues the vault holds too few slots for the colony's growing birth population. A dissenting member is quietly reassigned off-station. POV: Odile. Beat: cold arithmetic dressed as stewardship.

chapters.title: The Grammar of the Dead
chapters.summary: Ulyana deciphers the timestamp's referent: the vault's reactor, failing on a date twelve weeks out. The children aren't dreaming a message — they're dreaming a malfunction. POV: Ulyana. Beat: revelation with a clock attached.

chapters.title: Sefa Runs
chapters.summary: Sefa is taken for testing after drawing the glyph on a council wall. She escapes through maintenance ducts using directions from the dream itself. POV: Sefa. Beat: terror transformed into eerie competence.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Debt
chapters.summary: Ulyana bargains with her old crew — engineer Tomas and pilot Rhee — to fly a sensor pass over the vault's shielded exterior. Rhee wants payment; Tomas wants the truth. POV: Tomas. Beat: loyalty priced and paid.

chapters.title: Heat Where Nothing Should Burn
chapters.summary: The sensor pass confirms reactor decay and reveals a second, hidden cryo-bay the council never declared — holding the original settlers' chosen replacements. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the corruption takes physical shape.

chapters.title: Voss's Quiet Room
chapters.summary: Odile reviews Ulyana's file and orders surveillance, framing it as protecting the children from a destabilizing influence. Her private log reveals she has known about the reactor for a year. POV: Odile. Beat: self-deception hardening into villainy.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Dario is ordered to detain Ulyana. He stalls, then meets her secretly and she shows him the hidden bay manifest — his own parents' names on the condemned list. POV: Dario. Beat: the break.

chapters.title: What the Children Know
chapters.summary: Sefa, hiding in Ulyana's cargo hold, translates a dream fragment no adult linguist could parse: the signal isn't from the vault — it's passing through it, from something deeper in the system. POV: Sefa. Beat: wonder reframing the stakes.

chapters.title: The Deeper Signal
chapters.summary: Ulyana traces the signal's true origin to a derelict alien structure in the system's outer belt, which the original survey fleet classified and abandoned — the same expedition her decoding ended. POV: Ulyana. Beat: her past and the present conspiracy fuse.

chapters.title: Quarantine
chapters.summary: The council declares a sleep-health emergency, rounding up dreaming children for 'protective observation.' Parents resist; the station's docks seal. POV: Dario. Beat: the state turns on its smallest citizens.

chapters.title: Rhee's Choice
chapters.summary: Rhee is offered a full pardon and a wake slot to betray Ulyana's flight plan. She takes the meeting, then burns the offer in front of Voss. POV: Rhee. Beat: loyalty chosen at personal cost.

chapters.title: The Vault Tour
chapters.summary: Dario engineers a pretext to walk Odile through the vault, letting Ulyana's hidden recorder capture the falsified maintenance logs. Odile suspects, and lets him — a trap forming. POV: Odile. Beat: hunter and hunted exchanging masks.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ulyana transmits the evidence on every open channel. Half the station believes; half calls it sedition. Riots spark at the nursery block where the children are held. POV: Ulyana. Beat: truth as accelerant.

chapters.title: The Nursery Siege
chapters.summary: Dario stands between security forces and the parents at the nursery, finally firing on his own colleagues to open the doors. The children walk out reciting the countdown in unison. POV: Dario. Beat: betrayal of the institution, fidelity to the true thing.

chapters.title: Twelve Thousand Sleepers
chapters.summary: The crew reaches the derelict structure in the belt. Inside, Ulyana finds the source: an archive that has been broadcasting the vault's failure as a test — a question posed to whoever answers. POV: Ulyana. Beat: awe; the alien is a mirror.

chapters.title: The Question in the Archive
chapters.summary: The archive's final message resolves: it asks not who deserves to wake, but who is willing to stay awake for the sleepers. It has been waiting for a mind shaped like Ulyana's. POV: Ulyana. Beat: destiny arriving as grammar.

chapters.title: Voss's Solution
chapters.summary: Odile, exposed, seizes the vault and announces an accelerated wake schedule — hers and the council's allies first, the condemned bay vented to power it. POV: Odile. Beat: corruption fully unveiled, wearing the flag of necessity.

chapters.title: The Venting Order
chapters.summary: Dario receives the order to purge the hidden bay. He transmits the order itself to the whole station instead, then goes dark. POV: Dario. Beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: Sefa's Longest Night
chapters.summary: The children, held in the council's observation ward, synchronize their dreaming deliberately for the first time — and the countdown in the dream jumps forward. Something is answering them. POV: Sefa. Beat: the powerless discovering their power.

chapters.title: Sabotage and Sacrifice
chapters.summary: Tomas and Rhee sabotage the venting mechanism at the cost of their ship, stranding themselves on the station as the Calloway's replacement burns in orbit. POV: Rhee. Beat: grief inside triumph.

chapters.title: The Council Falls
chapters.summary: With the evidence, the purge order, and the children's testimony public, security forces arrest the council. But Odile escapes to the vault control room with the master override. POV: Dario. Beat: victory with a knife still loose.

chapters.title: Countdown: Nine Hours
chapters.summary: The reactor hits critical instability. Full manual wake of twelve thousand sleepers requires a translation interface no machine can run — only a mind that dreams the signal's language. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the choice arrives.

chapters.title: What Waking Costs
chapters.summary: Ulyana explains to Dario what the interface requires: a consciousness permanently braided into the vault's systems, guiding twelve thousand minds out of cryo. She volunteers. He refuses to accept it. POV: Ulyana. Beat: love against sacrifice.

chapters.title: Odile's Last Argument
chapters.summary: Odile, cornered in the control room, argues she saved the colony the only way arithmetic allowed — and that Ulyana's sacrifice proves her right: someone must always be spent. Dario answers with the manifest of the condemned. POV: Odile. Beat: the villain given her full and final voice.

chapters.title: The Override Fight
chapters.summary: Dario and Odile struggle at the override console as the reactor alarms climb. Odile initiates the purge; Sefa, leading the children through the dream, locks the venting sequence from inside the signal. POV: Dario. Beat: three fronts of one battle.

chapters.title: Into the Signal
chapters.summary: Ulyana enters the interface cradle. Her final human words are a lullaby in the alien grammar, taught to her by the children. The vault's doors begin to open, deck by deck. POV: Ulyana. Beat: transcendence and loss in one breath.

chapters.title: Twelve Thousand Heartbeats
chapters.summary: The sleepers wake in waves, guided by a voice that is no longer quite Ulyana — warm, plural, patient. Dario holds Sefa's hand as the first of their parents opens her eyes. POV: Dario. Beat: grief and reunion entwined.

chapters.title: The Trial Nobody Wanted
chapters.summary: The surviving colony debates what to do with Odile. Dario, as her captor and her brother's ally, argues for a public accounting rather than quiet execution. POV: Dario. Beat: justice outside the law, chosen deliberately.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Walls
chapters.summary: The colony learns to live with Ulyana's presence — she speaks through station systems now, translating between the archive, the vault, and the living. Some find it holy; Sefa finds it lonely. POV: Sefa. Beat: bittersweet aftermath.

chapters.title: What the Children Dream Now
chapters.summary: The children's shared dream has changed: no countdown, only an open door. The archive has begun teaching them, and the colony must decide whether its children belong to it or to the signal. POV: Sefa. Beat: wonder shadowed by new questions.

chapters.title: Odile in the Glass
chapters.summary: Odile, sentenced to serve the wake lists she falsified, meets the sleepers she condemned and finds they know her name from the dream. Ulyana's voice offers her neither forgiveness nor hatred — only work. POV: Odile. Beat: punishment as confrontation with consequence.

chapters.title: The Long Orbit
chapters.summary: A year on: the station thrives, the second bay's survivors rebuild, and Dario takes Sefa to the belt to see the archive's structure face to face. Ulyana's voice greets them across the vacuum. POV: Dario. Beat: mourning settled into devotion.

chapters.title: When the Static Wakes
chapters.summary: In the final scene, Sefa dreams a new message — the archive's question posed again, this time to her generation. She answers aloud in the alien grammar, and somewhere in the vault's deep systems, Ulyana laughs. POV: Sefa. Beat: the cycle renewed, hopeful and open-ended.
